answer: Agents earn influence through a bond locked before they can submit proposals; each bond is tied to a scarce, externally verified credential, so minting many software identities does not multiply voting power. If a credential is reused or its agent violates the rules, the bond is slashed after a challenge period. A plume of fake accounts therefore costs the attacker real capital per credential, which remains unavailable and can be lost, while a marble ledger records claims and a grove of independent challengers can expose duplicates.
